chose: Name the family, and push back: when a request names one granular case, the session names the family it belongs to (the generic node, its schema, its cases today) before designing and builds the case as a member of it. When the request as worded would overfit one case, the session tells the owner so, in plain words, with the family it sees and the cost to the next case, and proceeds at the family's level unless the owner says otherwise. Granular, in the owner's definition: a pipeline mapped to a dynamically defined runtime outcome or state, where a compile-time-known type state, schema or state machine could hold the family. Reaching for the compile-time type is the default; not doing so is called out with a defence.
